solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spooner’s rodent sounded like a top intricate nest-builder

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the phrase must be said with its initial sounds exchanged

blocks.note: a beaver is a large dam-building rodent; it lends its opening B to the second word and takes a W
a spinning top whirrs, so it whirred; it gives its W away and takes the B

explanation.surface: A strange zoological claim: some rodent made a noise just like a spinning top, and this creature builds elaborate nests.
explanation.walkthrough: Say BEAVER WHIRRED and swap the opening sounds: WEAVER BIRD. The 'bird' sound comes from 'whirred', not any spelt word.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaver birds are African finches famous for knotting grass into elaborate hanging nests, so the phrase describes them exactly.

clue.text: Cover wide pit perhaps, obscuring top

indicators.note: hiding the top of a down entry means its first letter is not seen

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide ball
a pit is one kind of trap; lose its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to throw a sheet over a broad hole in the ground so nobody falls in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a pit as an example of a TRAP; beheading it leaves RAP, and the cricket wide supplies W in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something is to enclose or cover it, as with paper around a present, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Honest write-ups disheartened son

indicators.note: losing one's heart means losing the central letters of the word

blocks.note: write-ups are ARTICLES; take out the middle pair IC
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Candid reports that have left a boy feeling dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTICLES has eight letters, so its heart is the central two, IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or cunning, which is being straightforward and sincere in character.

clue.text: Very old book – novel is set encompassing area in market town

indicators.note: as an adjective novel means new, so these letters take a fresh arrangement
to encompass is to surround, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: Eccles is a market town near Manchester, famous for its currant-filled Eccles cakes
taken as written, to be rearranged
A is the usual abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A literary note: an ancient volume, with a new story set around some district of a small English trading town.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits definition from wordplay; the jumbled IS SET wraps round A, and the whole sits after ECCLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament, written well over two thousand years ago, so it is certainly ancient scripture.

clue.text: Cursed naval commander heads for trouble evidently doomed

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, so only the leading letters are kept

blocks.note: Captain William Bligh commanded HMS Bounty when its crew mutinied
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A captain under a curse, whose troubles make it plain he is heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Bligh of the Bounty is the crossword's favourite naval commander; the famous mutiny makes 'cursed' and 'doomed' fit the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blighted has been spoiled or ruined as if by a curse or plague, so both adjectives describe damnation.

clue.text: Reoriented north-eastward avoiding the tors to move country

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so those letters are left out
the letters to be taken away are scattered, so they must be moved out wherever they sit
to reorient is to turn to face a new way, so what is left is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, with the hyphen dropped
these seven letters are removed one by one from the longer word, leaving N, A, W, A, R, D

explanation.surface: Directions for someone walking north-east across moorland to steer round the rocky hilltops.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak on a moor such as Dartmoor, so the surface feels like a hike. Striking T, H, E, T, O, R, S from the long word leaves six letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked nation in central East Africa, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Dispute criminal charges after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a rap sheet or taking the rap

explanation.surface: A defendant who, having thought it over, decides to contest the accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' reads as 'after thinking', but it means mirrored. Rap for a charge is American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or bicker, as boxers trade light blows, so it matches a verb meaning to argue.

clue.text: Plan military endeavour in writing

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another is in it, so a piece sits within a larger one

blocks.note: prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse
OP is short for a military operation

explanation.surface: Draw up a strategy for a campaign and put it down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for operation is the standard crossword shorthand; 'military' looks like it wants something longer, such as a campaign or sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to intend or put forward a scheme, as in 'I propose to leave early', so it matches the verb.

clue.text: Considering canned drink good

blocks.note: rum is a spirit made from sugar cane
something canned is in a tin, read as three short words
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Weighing up whether a drink from a can is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' seems to describe the drink, but it is its own piece: IN A TIN follows the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply or mull over, like a cow chewing cud, so it matches pondering.

clue.text: Reportedly, old citrus slicer is a let-down

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so what follows is taken by its sound

blocks.note: old is antique, the citrus fruit a lime, and a slicer an axe

explanation.surface: Someone digs out an ancient fruit-chopping gadget and finds it disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the three words together quickly and they merge into one long word.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing ending after a build-up of expectation, so it is precisely a disappointment.

clue.text: Supporting male model

blocks.note: to be for something is to support it
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man acting as a support model, perhaps in a fashion show or photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' looks like an adjective for the man, but it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A model can be a pattern or template, and form is used the same way, for shape or structure to follow.

clue.text: Making enquiries: monarch’s coming in when approximately?

indicators.note: arriving inside something means entering it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a king is a monarch; the 's stands for 'is'
around means roughly, as in 'around ten'

explanation.surface: Someone investigating wants to know roughly what time the sovereign is arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the monarch is coming into the two-letter word; the container here has nothing after it in AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking around means putting questions to various people to find something out, which is making inquiries.

clue.text: Carcass of moose on plain

indicators.note: a carcass is the shell of a body with its innards gone, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: the first and last letters
RE means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: The remains of a large deer lying on open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective meaning simple or bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child', which matches plain in the sense of simple or bare.

clue.text: Wrong date shown for stage musical

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre programme or poster has printed the wrong performance date for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is squarely theatrical, which hides the fact that the show's own title is the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadestown is a Tony-winning Broadway show by Anaïs Mitchell retelling Orpheus and Eurydice, so it is one example of theatre.

clue.text: One tends grave in light rain initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
placed within something, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to light something is to fire it, as in firing a kiln
the opening letter
grave and staid both mean sober and serious

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a burial plot, working in a gentle drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One tends' reads as a verb phrase about the grave, but it is a noun: one who tends. 'Light rain' also looks like a single idea (drizzle), yet the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-aider gives emergency care to the injured, so they are literally someone who tends people who are hurt.

clue.text: One knight observed keeping king motivated

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the chess notation for a knight
to spy is to observe
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A lone knight watched over his king and felt moved by it.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation K is taken by the king, so the knight is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inspired means being stirred or spurred into action or creativity, which matches being driven to act.

clue.text: Best penalties meeting back of net

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: fines are monetary penalties
the final letter

explanation.surface: A football report: the top penalty kicks are those that hit the rear of the goal net.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward spot kicks; here penalties are punishments paid in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Finest is the superlative of fine, meaning of the highest quality, the same as the top or greatest.

clue.text: Happy developing all of business, as one rogue gets dismissed

indicators.note: something developing is changing its shape, so the letters take a new arrangement
whatever is dismissed is sent away, so those letters are removed
rogue as an adjective means wayward, so the letters to be removed appear out of order

blocks.note: all three words taken as written
these five letters are struck out of the longer string wherever they fall

explanation.surface: A cheerful report of a firm that is growing as a single crooked employee is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All of' means every letter of the phrase, including the OF. The letters A, S, O, N, E leave scattered, and eight letters remain to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of great joy or contentment, which is an intensified form of being cheerful.

clue.text: Asian food starter of squid consumed in island country

indicators.note: a starter is the opening course, so only the first letter is kept
whatever is consumed ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific
the first letter

explanation.surface: A menu note: a squid appetiser eaten on a Pacific island alongside an Asian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' fits the food surface as a first course, but it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry parcel of spiced vegetables or meat from South Asian cuisine, so it is an Asian snack.

clue.text: The German leaves rambling message

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: rambling talk or paths meander
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German speaker walks out of a long, wandering communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' could be a noun (tree leaves), but it is a verb here. DER goes from the middle of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: The meaning of something is its import or point, which is what 'the message' of a film or text also refers to.

clue.text: Following delay, depressed signal to stop

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lag is a delay, as in time lag
to feel down is to be depressed

explanation.surface: After a hold-up, someone feeling low gives a sign that they want to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' reads as 'after', but it is the single letter F used in page references (p. 12f).
explanation.definitionFit: To flag down a vehicle is to wave at it so the driver halts, as with a taxi.

clue.text: Deliveries of the French wine ultimately late

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end
du is French for 'of the'
the final letter

explanation.surface: Shipments of French wine have arrived behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' feels like parcels, but it is the cricket term: an over is six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means not arrived or done by the expected time, which is simply behind time.

clue.text: This plant confused with fern might be in some farm

indicators.note: confused things are mixed up, so these letters are a jumble of another set
the answer only makes the full set once another word is added, so that word comes off again

blocks.note: taken as written: ten letters to be jumbled
taken as written, then taken back out of the jumble

explanation.surface: A gardening note: a plant, easily mistaken for a fern, could be growing on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the answer plus FERN together rearrange to IN SOME FARM. Mimosa's feathery leaves do look fern-like, which makes the surface true.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a genus of shrubs with feathery leaves, including the sensitive plant, so it is a real plant.

clue.text: Schools struggling aimed to invest in experts

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so these letters are rearranged
to invest in is to put inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: aces are experts, as in a flying ace
taken as written

explanation.surface: Failing schools set out to put money into specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest in' has its financial sense on the surface, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: In England, academies are state-funded schools run independently of local councils, so they are a type of school.

clue.text: Cycling, catch winged beast

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the letters rotate, the end coming to the front

blocks.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: Out on a bike, someone manages to catch a flying creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the last letter of HEAR to the front. The rhea has wings, though it cannot fly, so 'winged' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, related to the ostrich, so it is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Commercials broadcast for supplements

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: ads are short for advertisements

explanation.surface: Advertisements on TV or radio promoting health supplements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits commercials on the surface. 'Supplements' is a verb here, not the pills.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplement something is to add to it, so the verb in the third person matches exactly.

clue.text: Welshman’s raised platform

blocks.note: Dai is a common Welsh man's name, a Welsh form of David
the possessive S, taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage belonging to a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use Dai as the typical Welshman, just as Ian is a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a low stage at the front of a hall for speakers or dignitaries, so it is an elevated stand.

clue.text: Prisoner based at sea

blocks.note: a con is a convict
founded on something is based on it

explanation.surface: A convict kept aboard a ship, like a prisoner on a hulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' pretends to be a location, but it is the idiom for bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being confused and lost, and confounded means baffled or perplexed.

clue.text: Have a tantrum close to dinner time

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A hungry child throws a fit when the evening meal is near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near', but it means the end of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to shout and storm in fury, which is what someone throwing a fit does.

clue.text: Sickly-looking state of some from agencies, send ill applicants back

indicators.note: only some of the letters are taken from the words that follow, as a run within them
going back means running in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the final S of the first word, the next two words whole, and the opening AP of the last

explanation.surface: Agencies are told to turn away candidates who are unwell, with a remark on their peaky appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles four words and reads right to left, which is why the surface can mention illness so openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallidness is paleness of complexion, the washed-out look of someone unwell, so it is an unhealthy appearance.
